system.name: Ditto
system.one_liner: the first caching system built for disaggregated memory, using a client-centric framework and adaptive caching to keep hit rates high as resources change

content.subject: how adaptive caching picks an eviction victim from expert candidates and updates expert weights after a cache-miss regret signal

elements.name: Eviction Process
elements.role: dashed-boundary title for the left phase: proposing candidates, picking a victim, logging it

elements.name: Adaptive Process
elements.role: dashed-boundary title for the right phase: detecting a miss and updating expert weights

elements.name: LRU List (Expert 1)
elements.role: first caching expert's own data structure, used to propose an eviction candidate

elements.name: LFU Heap (Expert 2)
elements.role: second caching expert's own data structure, used to propose an eviction candidate

elements.role: the single candidate chosen, weighted by expert performance, to actually be evicted

elements.name: Eviction Hist.
elements.role: fixed-size FIFO queue recording each evicted object's ID and which expert(s) proposed it

elements.name: Miss Key
elements.role: the ID of an object that was requested but missed in the cache, looked up against the eviction history

elements.role: per-expert weight table (w_LRU, w_LFU) biasing victim selection and updated by miss regret

steps.what: each expert proposes an eviction candidate from its own caching data structure
steps.carries: a candidate object ID per expert

steps.what: a victim is chosen opportunistically among the candidates, weighted by each expert's current performance weight
the victim's object ID and the expert(s) that proposed it are inserted into the fixed-size FIFO eviction history

content.key_idea: Multiple caching experts propose eviction candidates; a weight-biased choice picks the victim and logs it, and a later miss on a logged object is a regret that lowers the responsible expert's weight.
content.reading_order: left to right and back: step 1 from the two expert data structures into Candidates, 2 into Eviction Victim (biased by Weights), 3 into Eviction Hist., 4 across to Miss Key, 5 back up into Weights

summary: Figure 8 walks through Ditto's multi-armed-bandit adaptive caching mechanism on a monolithic server, in five numbered steps. In the Eviction Process (left), two caching experts, an LRU List and an LFU Heap, each propose an eviction candidate from their own data structure (1); the current per-expert Weights bias which candidate becomes the actual Eviction Victim (2); that victim's object ID and proposing expert(s) are logged into a fixed-size FIFO Eviction Hist. queue (3). In the Adaptive Process (right), a later cache miss's key is looked up in the eviction history (4); if found there, a regret is registered and the weight of whichever expert (w_LRU or w_LFU) evicted that object is decreased (5), so the better-performing caching policy gradually gains more influence over future victim choices.
summary_zh: 该图分5步走读Ditto自适应缓存(MAB)：①LRU/LFU两专家各提候选；②按权重选出Eviction Victim；③记入Eviction Hist.队列；④未命中时查该历史(Miss Key)；⑤命中则降低对应专家权重。
